core_concepts: Ongoing substernal pain at rest with arm radiation and major cardiovascular risk factors must be treated as possible acute coronary syndrome until urgent assessment excludes it.
ACS includes unstable angina, NSTEMI, and STEMI; symptoms alone do not reliably distinguish them.
Initial evaluation requires urgent ECG-based assessment and cardiac troponin testing within an emergency pathway; treatment then depends on ACS subtype, bleeding risk, and reperfusion strategy.
diagnostic_clues: Two hours of pain at rest
Substernal pain radiating to the left arm
Hypertension, diabetes, smoking, and family history of myocardial infarction
common_misconceptions: Antacid response or non-response is not enough to confirm or exclude ACS.
A patient describing pain as heartburn does not make a gastrointestinal diagnosis safe.
Absence of every classic symptom does not rule out ACS.
dangerous_errors: Reassuring or discharging the patient as reflux before urgent ACS evaluation
Delaying emergency escalation while completing a routine outpatient history
Claiming that a single symptom, ECG, or troponin result always rules ACS in or out
management_principles: Escalate promptly to an acute chest-pain/ACS pathway and monitor the patient.
Use ECG, serial troponin assessment, and the full clinical context rather than one symptom in isolation.
Use antithrombotic and reperfusion strategies according to the working diagnosis, contraindications, bleeding risk, and local emergency protocol.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Exact drug selection, dose, and invasive timing depend on ECG findings, troponin results, contraindications, bleeding risk, and local protocol.
Other immediately dangerous causes of chest pain, including aortic dissection and pulmonary embolism, remain in the differential when supported by the presentation.

source_refs.title: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for Acute Coronary Syndromes

reference_soap.subjective: 58M presenting with 2hr substernal chest pain 7/10, radiating to left arm, onset at rest. Denies relief with antacids. PMH: HTN, T2DM. Smokes 20 pack-years.
reference_soap.assessment: ACS until proven otherwise. DDx: STEMI, NSTEMI, unstable angina, aortic dissection, PE.
reference_soap.plan: Urgent acute chest-pain/ACS pathway with monitoring, ECG and serial troponin assessment; give aspirin when appropriate and not contraindicated, provide oxygen only if clinically indicated for hypoxemia, establish IV access, and obtain urgent cardiology/emergency input. Further antithrombotic and reperfusion management depends on findings, contraindications, bleeding risk, and local protocol.

learning_objectives: Elicit cardiac history systematically using SOCRATES
Explore cardiac risk factors: HTN, DM, smoking, family Hx, dyslipidaemia
Address patient's ICE — especially fear of MI
Verbalize ACS differential and dangerous diagnosis first

teaching.one_liner: Chest pain from a blocked or critically narrowed coronary artery — the one diagnosis you must exclude first in any adult with chest pain.
red_flags: Pain lasting over 20 minutes at rest, sweating, low blood pressure, or fainting

must_ask.objective: Site and radiation of the pain
must_ask.say: Where exactly is the pain, and does it move anywhere else?
When did it start, and how long does it last each time?
How would you describe it — sharp, crushing, burning, tight?
Along with the pain, did you feel sweaty, sick, or short of breath?
Do you have high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol, and do you smoke?

must_ask.objective: Family history of early heart disease
must_ask.say: Has anyone in your family had a heart attack, especially young?
What are you most worried this might be?

history.answer: I have had this terrible pressure and aching in my chest for the past two hours, and it will not go away.
It started suddenly about two hours ago while I was sitting quietly on the couch watching television.
It is right in the middle of my chest behind the breastbone, and it feels broad rather than something I can point to with a finger.
It feels like a heavy, crushing tightness, as if someone placed a heavy weight on my chest.
Yes, the dull ache spreads down my left arm all the way to my wrist, but not into my jaw or back.
It has been completely constant for the entire two hours since it started, without any breaks.
It is around a seven out of ten in severity, and it has stayed steady at that intensity.
I was resting when it hit me, and staying still has not helped ease the pain at all.
Taking a deep breath, coughing, or moving around does not change the pain in any way.
Pressing on my ribs or chest does not make the pain any worse.
I had lunch hours earlier, but I tried taking some antacid tablets when the pain started, and they gave me no relief whatsoever.
I broke out in a sudden cold sweat and have been feeling nauseated, along with a bit of shortness of breath.
No, I have not passed out or felt dizzy or lightheaded.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, cough, or phlegm.
No, I have been completely well without any colds, sore throat, or body aches recently.
No swelling or aching in my legs, and I have not had any recent surgeries, long trips, or bed rest.
No, there are no rashes, bumps, or blisters anywhere on my skin.
I feel very frightened and anxious, like something terrible is happening inside my body.
No, I have never had chest pain like this before, and I have never had heart procedures or stents.
No, I have not had any falls, blows to the chest, or heavy lifting recently.
I was wondering if it could just be severe indigestion or heartburn, but the antacids did not help at all.
I am terrified that this is a heart attack because my father died of a heart attack when he was sixty-two.
I really need you to give me something to relieve this terrible pain and figure out what is wrong.
I have had high blood pressure for five years and type 2 diabetes for three years.
I have never had any surgeries, and I have never stayed overnight in a hospital.
I take metformin 1000 mg twice a day for diabetes and lisinopril 10 mg once a day for blood pressure.
No, I do not have any allergies to medications or foods.
I have smoked about a pack of cigarettes a day for twenty years.
I drink about two beers every evening.
I am retired and live at home with my wife.
My father had a fatal heart attack at age sixty-two, and my mother had high blood pressure.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 142/88 mmHg without difference between arms, heart rate 84 beats per minute, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, and temperature 36.8°C.
Anxious-appearing man clutching his chest with noticeable diaphoresis and mild pallor, but in no respiratory distress.
Skin is cool and clammy with no rashes, vesicles, or erythema across the chest wall.
Jugular venous pressure is normal without distension or abnormal pulsations.
No chest wall deformity, and firm palpation across the sternum and costochondral junctions reproduces no tenderness.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2, and no murmurs, gallops, or pericardial friction rubs.
Resonant to percussion symmetrically throughout all lung fields.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without wheezing, crackles, or rhonchi.
Abdomen is soft, non-distended, and non-tender, including the epigastrium, without guarding or rebound tenderness.
No pitting edema in either lower extremity.
Both calves are symmetric, soft, non-tender, and without warmth or palpable cords.
